origin.discovery_context: While remediating the MT-004/005/009 CRDT fail-closed admission path, a closed constraint loop was found and independently confirmed by direct source inspection that makes a Proposal-kind CRDT-bearing ModelLaneMessage UN-ADMITTABLE at HEAD: no crdt_proposal_ref row can ever satisfy the resolver's applied_update_sha256 == kernel_crdt_updates.update_sha256 cross-check, because the two hashes are computed over different byte encodings of the same edit.
origin.operator_directive: Operator instruction 2026-07-23/24: 'if you see unexpected future gaps or work address it inside the same MT or defer it if this does not correlate with the current MT to a future MT in the same WP so we do not forget to address it.' This gap crosses into the knowledge-CRDT pillar (migration + spec touch) so it is deferred here rather than fixed inside MT-004/005/009.
origin.layer_1_already_shipped: MT-004/005/009 V5 shipped the Layer-1 sync-layer fix in validate_message_authority (model_lane.rs): CRDT posture completeness is no longer required unconditionally on every crdt_* field, so a real Status-kind CRDT message backed by a real Yjs update + real snapshot + active lease is now admissible, and the kind-aware durable proposal-ref rule at validate_message_crdt_authority_tx is no longer dead code. Layer-2 (this MT) is the remaining spec-level fix for the Proposal-kind path only.

scope.summary: Resolve the diff-hash vs Yjs-update-hash conflation that makes an approved-proposal-backed (Proposal-kind) CRDT ModelLaneMessage un-admittable, so proposal-anchored CRDT authority can be proven end-to-end.
scope.root_cause: apply_approved_ai_edit (src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/ai_edit_proposal.rs ~665-691) computes applied_content_sha256 = sha256(serde_json::to_vec(applied_diff)) — a hash of the JSON diff object. bind_applied_ai_edit_update (src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/knowledge_crdt.rs ~1562-1586) and migration 0192's CHECK force applied_update_sha256 = diff_sha256, i.e. that same JSON hash. But resolve_model_lane_crdt_authority_tx (src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs ~13011,13073-13085) requires the referenced kernel_crdt_updates row to satisfy BOTH sha256(update_bytes) == update_sha256 AND Update::decode_v1(update_bytes) succeeds — i.e. update_sha256 is the hash of the Yjs v1 BINARY update. Then the proposal cross-check (~13784-13793) requires proposal.applied_update_sha256 == resolved.update_sha256. Equating a JSON-object hash with a Yjs-binary hash is unsatisfiable short of a SHA-256 collision, so no honest proposal row can ever back an admitted CRDT message.
forbidden_paths: weakening any resolver fail-closed gate to make the loop close
acceptance_criteria: The proposal->applied->CRDT-update authority trail is internally consistent: the value the resolver cross-checks binds the proposal to the REAL kernel_crdt_updates row by identity (applied_update_id) and verifies that row's own integrity (its update_sha256 over the Yjs binary), rather than requiring a JSON-diff hash to equal a Yjs-update hash.

A Proposal-kind ModelLaneMessage that references an approved+applied proposal whose applied update is a real persisted Yjs update is ADMITTED by validate_message_crdt_authority_tx and replays with all applicable crdt_* fields intact.

Every existing fail-closed denial is preserved: fabricated update ref, hash mismatch on the Yjs bytes, stale/unrelated state vector, wrong actor/session/trace/workspace/document identity, un-approved review_state, missing applied binding, and duplicate/idempotency conflicts all still fail closed with their specific denial reasons.

The change is expressed as a governed migration (copy-forward, never in-place edit of 0192) plus the minimal Rust change; migration 0192's intent is preserved or superseded with an explicit note, not silently broken.

If SPEC_CURRENT names durable CRDT applied-binding authority semantics, the spec is enriched via the copy-first indexed-bundle workflow in the same change (CX-105B/C); if it is silent, record an ASSUMPTION/PROVISIONAL DECISION local to this MT and flag it for operator spec review.

MT-002 CRDT-targeting positive proof, the MT-009 converge proof target (mixed_model_lane_integration_pg_tests::mt009_real_postgres_yjs_updates_compaction_receipts_and_lane_state_converge), and the MT-005 lease-denial probe (model_lane_context_bundle_pg_tests::model_lane_context_bundle_crdt_state_vector_and_loom_refs_are_replayable) all pass on real Handshake-managed PostgreSQL using ONE canonical reusable admissible-CRDT-message helper.
Post-implementation adversarial review confirms the proposal path cannot be spoofed by an internally inconsistent proposal row (the exact anti-pattern this MT removes must remain impossible).
scope.risk_if_missed: MT-002/005/009 CRDT admission retains ZERO positive end-to-end proof: the Proposal-kind CRDT authority path can never be exercised, so a whole class of the ModelLane CRDT contract is asserted only by negative tests. A future implementer may 'fix' the failing tests by fabricating an inconsistent proposal row, silently defeating the fail-closed design this WP exists to establish.

implementation_notes: Preferred direction (verify against spec + code before choosing): bind and cross-check on applied_update_id (identity) and verify the referenced kernel_crdt_updates row's OWN integrity (sha256(update_bytes)==update_sha256 + Update::decode_v1) independently, instead of requiring proposal.applied_update_sha256 to equal the Yjs update hash. The proposal's own content integrity (diff_sha256 over the JSON diff) stays a separate, still-enforced invariant.
Do NOT relax any resolver gate to make the loop close; the fix is to stop conflating two distinct hashes, not to drop a check.
Migration discipline: never edit 0192 in place; add a forward migration and document whether 0192's applied_update_sha256=diff_sha256 CHECK is superseded, retained, or replaced, with reasoning.

Build ONE reusable admissible-CRDT-message test helper (real persisted Yjs update + real base snapshot + active lease with matching actor/session/trace identity; update session_id == lane session_id; lease correlation_id == update trace_id) and use it for every positive CRDT admission proof so future tests stop hand-rolling partial/synthetic postures.
If this MT changes any product behavior, storage/event contract, or diagnostic surface, update the in-product UserManual in the same change per HBR-MAN-004.
Rust-only backend change plus governed migration; PostgreSQL/EventLedger authority only; no SQLite.

risks: A lazy fix drops the resolver cross-check entirely, admitting any proposal ref.
A migration edits 0192 in place and breaks historical applied-binding rows.
The reusable helper hard-codes an identity shortcut that a real caller could not reproduce, re-creating a scaffold-only proof.
minimum_controls: Keep every existing denial test green; add a negative test proving an internally inconsistent proposal row (JSON-hash != real update hash but pointed at a real update id) is still refused.
Forward-only migration with explicit 0192 disposition note.
Helper builds authority exclusively through real product APIs (apply_approved_ai_edit path or its governed equivalent), never by raw INSERT of an inconsistent row.

handshake_compatibility.spec_realism_gate: Implementer may move only to READY_FOR_VALIDATION after the three real-PG proof targets pass against the Handshake-managed cluster; COMPLETED is validator-only.
